title: TS-22 Voice understanding and voice messages route
description:
## Slice 2 ticket 22 of 40, phase notes: paths use `conversation/` (the workspace as it is on develop). Design source: `git show origin/docs/typescript-control-plane:docs/TYPESCRIPT_CONTROL_PLANE.md` (section 8, row 22); read sections 0.3, 2, 3 and 6 as needed. Read AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md first. Never read or write `project/`; use `kbs` only.

## Goal
Port the understand-the-user step and POST voice-messages. The understanding step is one non-durable model call outside a Harness; its call shape is unverified.

## Kind
prototype-first: a library API in this ticket is uncertain. A Sonnet agent must FIRST produce verified, runnable code for it (see Prototype section), paste it into this ticket as a comment, and ONLY THEN is the ticket completed with that code verbatim. A Haiku implementer must not start the build part until that comment exists; if it is missing, stop and report.

## Branch and commit
```text
git fetch origin
git switch -c ts/22-voice-understanding-and-voice-messages-r origin/develop
...work, then...
git add <only the files listed under Files>
git commit -m "feat(conversation): voice understanding and voice messages route

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
git push -u origin ts/22-voice-understanding-and-voice-messages-r
```
Do NOT open a pull request; the orchestrator opens it. Commit messages contain no emojis.

## Files to create or change
- `conversation/src/voice/understanding.ts`
- `conversation/src/http/routes/voice-messages.ts`
- `conversation/features-support/steps/voice.steps.ts`

## Exported interface and error behavior
`understandUtterance(deps, {transcript, recentMessages}): Promise<{kind: "post" | "filler"; body: string}>`; model gpt-5-nano, minimal reasoning, JSON output, prompt text copied exactly from understanding.py. Participant checks run before the paid call. Replay by Idempotency-Key returns the earlier result with `degraded: false`. Spend recorded with `turn_id = "voice:<uuid>"`.

General rules: TypeScript ESM, `.ts` import suffixes as in conversation/src/storage/; tabs for indentation as in existing files; long clear names; no line comments; TSDoc on exported symbols; no emojis. Each Python exception class used by a ported function becomes an exported `Error` subclass with the same name and the same message text. Failures are thrown, never returned as magic values, unless the Python returned them.

## Python source to port (keep structure; read it fully before writing)
- `python/src/chatticus/voice/understanding.py (274 lines; two commits)`
- `docs/VOICE.md (the rules)`
Rule: mechanical ports keep the Python file's structure and cite the Python line range in the commit body. Behavior that no scenario encodes is still kept.

## Prototype (must be done and pasted before the build)
A Sonnet agent proves how to make a single JSON-mode completion with @earendil-works/pi-ai outside a Harness against a scripted provider (or, if awkward, with the `openai` package that pi-ai depends on), returning the parsed JSON and usage. Pasted into the ticket and used verbatim.

## Behavior spec (Gherkin, ported unchanged)
Existing features that must pass under cucumber-js when this ticket closes. Do NOT edit these `.feature` files except where this ticket says a behavior changed.

### features/voice_messages.feature

### features/web_voice_control.feature
Scenarios: A line said in a teammate's conversation goes to that teammate; In a named channel, a line goes to the teammate chosen to answer; Nothing is sent when no conversation is open; Saying stop listening turns the microphone off; A line said while the teammate is working is queued and sent when the turn ends; Several lines said while the teammate is working are delivered in order as one message; Queued lines are dropped, and the member is told, when the conversation changes; A line said while the teammate is idle is sent at once; A speaking state that is stuck does not discard later lines; A reply still sounding past its expected end still guards against the browser hearing itself; A line that could not be sent is spoken aloud; A line the server found no message in is spoken aloud; A line that could not be checked against the teammate is spoken aloud; A line discarded as an echo while no reply is playing is spoken aloud; Echo feedback heard back does not trigger more feedback; A failed send keeps the line and retries it with the next line; Echo feedback followed by a send failure still speaks the failure; Send-failure feedback during a reply is spoken after the reply ends; A parked failure retries on its own after 5 seconds; With the server down the failure is spoken once and retried once; Several notices that waited for a reply are spoken together once; A line heard with no conversation open is spoken aloud; Spoken feedback never talks over a reply; Voice listening needs a cross-origin isolated page; Voice listening needs a microphone; A teammate's reply is spoken when their turn ends while listening; Only the reply is spoken, never the teammate's name; Nothing is spoken while listening is off; The spoken reply is the teammate's own answer to that turn; Formatting, links and code are spoken as plain words; A long reply is cut short with a pointer to the screen; A failed turn's reason is spoken; Saying stop while a reply is being spoken stops speaking; While a reply is being spoken, other speech is ignored; The tail of a spoken reply heard after it ends is not acted on; After a spoken reply ends, the next line goes to the same teammate; A reply whose end is never reported stops blocking the member after its expected length; A reply whose end is never reported still guards against the browser hearing itself; A line is placed in time by the clock, not by the recognizer's own timeline; The voice button always says what the session is doing; A speech recognition hiccup does not end the voice conversation; Capture keeps listening while a reply is being spoken; Capture that stops delivering audio is noticed whether or not a reply is spoken; A suspended capture engine is noticed; A muted microphone track is not treated as listening; An ended microphone track is not treated as listening; Capture that comes back on its own after a wake-up says it is listening again; Capture that does not come back is restarted from a fresh microphone stream; A muted track that a wake-up does not fix is restarted; When a restart needs a tap, the button asks for one and the tap resumes listening; A line heard during a reply that is not a stop command does not stop the reply; The watchdog does not end speech that has not started yet; The watchdog ends speech that never starts after a grace period; The watchdog ends speech that started and then went quiet; The watchdog never ends speech the engine is still producing; Speech that ended early says why; Speech that finished on its own says nothing; Tapping opens the microphone and audio context before any await so the tap still counts as the gesture; Capture that keeps stalling after restarts stops cycling and asks for a tap; A capture engine suspended by a spoken reply is left alone until speech ends; Stalled audio frames during a spoken reply are not acted on until speech ends

Steps call `this.api` (HTTP via `app.request()`) for HTTP steps and the same domain functions the routes call for direct steps; steps never reach into a store.
Step file(s) to write: under `conversation/features-support/steps/` as named in Files above (at most about 400 lines each; split by subject).

## Stop rules
If anything in this ticket is wrong, ambiguous, impossible, or contradicted by the code you find (a Python line range does not match, a step has no Python match, a library API differs from what is written, a scenario cannot pass without changing its text), STOP and report to the orchestrator with the exact file, line and observation.
